title: Casa Cardona  / Sensacional Dinámica Mexicana
text:
Casa Cardona / Sensacional Dinámica Mexicana

Initially conceived as a conventional 165 m² real estate development, the residence demonstrates how an architectural proposal can transcend commercial parameters to create spatial, cultural, and human value. Its architecture establishes an intimate dialogue with the desert, transforming the conditions of its surroundings into a distinctive domestic experience.

title: Project MMR / David Ito Arquitetura
text:
Project MMR / David Ito Arquitetura

The MMR House was designed for a young couple who brought several highly specific demands to the project. Among them were the desire for a spiral staircase inside the house, the presence of a tree integrated into the interior environment, the ability to see the slope of the roof from the inside, and the creation of a double-height space. In addition, there were general programmatic requirements: four suites, an office, spacious social areas prepared to host around forty people, strong integration with nature, and, at the same time, privacy from the gated community.

title: Santa Rosa Social Housing / FAR frohn&rojas
text:
Santa Rosa Social Housing / FAR frohn&rojas

In recent decades, rising land prices have pushed much of Santiago's social housing to the urban periphery, creating settlements that are often disconnected from social and technical infrastructure.

title: Coqueira House / Tiago Sousa Arquitecto
text:
Coqueira House / Tiago Sousa Arquitecto

Geometry, planes and a suspended volume. The site is organised into two distinct levels. The upper level comprises the majority of the site and is accessed via the upper road. The lower level, on the other hand, is the result of an excavation, connected to the lower road, and is a flat platform contained between large granite retaining walls.

title: Ironwood Retreat / The Ranch Mine
text:
Ironwood Retreat / The Ranch Mine

Most of Arizona's streams run only after a storm. Oak Creek is one of the few that flows all year and the water changes everything around it. Along its banks in Sedona, Arizona, sycamores, cottonwoods, ash and alder grow into a canopy of shade and green that most of the state never sees. On a wooded bend of the creek, architecture firm The Ranch Mine has designed "Ironwood," a small retreat built around one simple wish: to spend the days and nights down by the water, under the trees.

title: Dondoh Restaurant / Costa + Herrera Arquitectos
text:
Dondoh Restaurant / Costa + Herrera Arquitectos

Dondoh is Chile's first Japanese grill. This venue, recently opened in the Chilean capital, stands out for its imposing design inspired by Japan's ancient Izakayas. Elements such as wood, stone, and fire serve as the main protagonists. Dondoh refers to an ancient Japanese ceremony performed by farmers around the year 1500, invoking the God of Fire. The God of Fire would warm the Earth so that seeds could germinate. The fire was fed with small wooden tablets, and the flames rose along with the prayers written upon them.

title: MOKUZAI / IT'S Studio
text:
MOKUZAI / IT'S Studio

Mokuzai is an office building that includes public health services, featuring a mixed timber and concrete structure designed by IT'S.

title: The City as a Quarry: Housing Transformation
text:
The City as a Quarry: Housing Transformation

The City as a Quarry: Housing Transformation brings together representatives of the European Commission and the Government of Catalonia with European architects to explore how the renovation, reuse and transformation of existing buildings can help increase housing supply in response to the housing crisis and the climate emergency.

Curated by architects Marta Peris and José Toral of PERIS+TORAL Arquitectes, the event examines the conversion of offices and commercial premises, the renovation and extension of residential buildings, and the reuse of structures and materials. Discussions will address public policy, financing, regulation and architectural practice.

The event is part of the series Contemporary Catalan

title: Planned Overflow: How Singapore Balances Floods, Canals, and Public Space
text:
Planned Overflow: How Singapore Balances Floods, Canals, and Public Space

At Bishan–Ang Mo Kio Park in Singapore, a river does not occupy a fixed boundary. Under ordinary conditions, water moves through a naturalized channel bordered by grass, planting, and paths that bring visitors close to the river. During heavy rainfall, water spreads into the surrounding park, which is designed to accommodate flows beyond the capacity of the narrower channel. What appears to be a public landscape is also working infrastructure. Singapore's approach retains drainage engineering while assigning a wider role to the land around it.

title: Muammer Karaca Theatre Refurbishment / Novos Studio
text:
Muammer Karaca Theatre Refurbishment / Novos Studio

Located in the heart of Beyoğlu, Muammer Karaca Theatre was founded in 1955 by Muammer Karaca, a leading figure of Turkish boulevard theatre, and designed by architect Perran Doğancı. Situated on a cul-de-sac opening onto İstiklal Avenue, the theatre remained an important part of Istanbul's cultural life for more than half a century.

title: Politecnica, Park Associati, and AMDL CIRCLE Win Competition for Cultural Hub in Italy’s UNESCO-Listed Valle Camonica
text:
Politecnica, Park Associati, and AMDL CIRCLE Win Competition for Cultural Hub in Italy’s UNESCO-Listed Valle Camonica

A team led by Politecnica Building for Humans, with Park Associati and AMDL CIRCLE as architectural co-leads and Studio Mattioli responsible for geology and archaeology, has won the competition for a new cultural hub in Ceto, Italy. The project will transform the former Società Filati Niggeler & Kupfer textile mill into a facility comprising exhibition spaces, research facilities, an auditorium, and visitor services. Located in Valle Camonica, an area known for its prehistoric rock engravings, the proposal approaches the site through the relationship between industrial heritage, archaeology, and the surrounding landscape.

title: HOUSE JCM / Ralph Germann architectes
text:
HOUSE JCM / Ralph Germann architectes

The original building was a barn, with hay stored on the upper floor and the ground floor used as temporary accommodation by the farmer at the time. The rather steep pitch of the original roof allowed snow to slide off. The very deep eaves protected the façade from the elements. The original triangular openings provided ventilation for the barn to preserve the hay; during the renovation they were retained and fitted with glazing.

title: Stefano Boeri Architetti Selected to Transform Former Locomotive Factory into Green Neighbourhood in Tbilisi
text:
Stefano Boeri Architetti Selected to Transform Former Locomotive Factory into Green Neighbourhood in Tbilisi

The LOCO Alliance architectural competition in Tbilisi, Georgia, was organized to transform a 73,600 m² brownfield site, the former Soviet-era Tbilisi Electric Locomotive Manufacturing Plant in the "Temka" residential area, into a new green neighborhood and cultural destination called Loco Park. On October 18, 2026, LOCO Alliance officially announced Stefano Boeri Architetti's design as the selected project for the site's transformation, with the official masterplan images unveiled on October 23. The selected masterplan is designed to integrate the industrial heritage of the factory with contemporary architecture, dense green public spaces and community recreation hubs. The site is already hosting large-scale cultural events, organized in parallel with the formal masterplan competition.

title: Building the View: 4 Brazilian Houses Framing the Sea
text:
Building the View: 4 Brazilian Houses Framing the Sea

Throughout history, people have sought ways to see the world. In Renaissance painting, linear perspective made this impulse explicit by transforming the canvas into a window, organizing depth from a fixed viewpoint. In his treatise De Pictura (1435), Leon Battista Alberti described painting as a window onto what one wishes to represent. Landscape, in this sense, ceased to be simply what lay before the eyes and became a visual construction, a reality selected and organized by the gaze.

title: Mornington House / Foomann Architects
text:
Mornington House / Foomann Architects

Mornington House is our clients' holiday home. It sits on the same block as an older holiday home, occupied by their adult children and families, and shares a swimming pool and driveway. The couple engaged Foomann to design a relaxed house that focuses on the view, where they can host guests and entertain.

title: House in Mibu / Tato Architects
text:
House in Mibu / Tato Architects

Through architecture, we inevitably alter the environment. Yet we are always asking whether that act of alteration might avoid damaging its surroundings, whether it might instead change them in a way that heals.

title: How Material Choices Shape Contemporary Additions to Historic Buildings
text:
How Material Choices Shape Contemporary Additions to Historic Buildings

Adding new floors on top of a historic building presents a challenge beyond accommodating additional space: how can a contemporary intervention respond to the character of an existing structure? Material selection plays an important role in establishing a relationship between different construction periods, whether the aim is to complement the existing building or create a more distinct architectural expression. The LH Residence in Varna, Bulgaria, designed by STARH, offers an example of how fiber cement can help relate a contemporary addition to a historic building.

title: SIP Coffee and Bakery / movs studio
text:
SIP Coffee and Bakery / movs studio

SIP is a coffee and bakery shop in a shopping mall in Almaty, Kazakhstan, designed by MOVS STUDIO. A mall is a place of constant movement, with crowds, music, and bright shopfronts competing for attention, and the studio set out to give visitors a short rest from all of it. The name already holds the idea: a sip is a small, unhurried act, and the interior turns it into a place to slow down.

title: Creasvalley CC Clubhouse / LJL Architects
text:
Creasvalley CC Clubhouse / LJL Architects

Even an artificially constructed site can become a landscape as time accumulates. Topography, vegetation, light, and seasonal change establish a distinct order, within which architecture takes its place. The clubhouse is conceived not as an object from which to view its surroundings, but as a mediator through which the site is experienced through terrain, sightlines, and the relationship between inside and outside. The design began by observing this inherent order and exploring how architecture could engage with it.

title: Montana Farm / Estudio Balzano
text:
Montana Farm / Estudio Balzano

Montana Farm is a boutique equestrian breeding and training facility located in Buenos Aires, Argentina, dedicated to the selective breeding and high-level training of show jumping horses. The project was conceived to integrate architecture, landscape, and the specific needs of horses within a contemporary equestrian complex, prioritizing animal welfare, functionality, and spatial quality.

title: Relámpago House  / h3o architects
text:
Relámpago House / h3o architects

The house, with a gable roof, is characterized by the materialization of lightning as a central element that defines and separates the interior spaces. The lightning, when transformed into a wall and luminaire, clearly and immediately structures and shapes the functioning of the different rooms.

title: Ombria Hotel and Apartments Loulé / PROMONTORIO
text:
Ombria Hotel and Apartments Loulé / PROMONTORIO

Quinta da Ombria is a property in the Algarve hinterland with 150 hectares. Surrounded by extensive citrus groves, fig and carob trees, small farms and villages, the dramatic landscape and the rich biodiversity of this mountainous estate comprise a watercourse and a series of archaeological remnants related to farming and its early waterworks. The resort comprises golf course, hotel and clubhouse, in addition to villas and other residential units.

title: Dunhua Tower / Oyler Wu Collaborative
text:
Dunhua Tower / Oyler Wu Collaborative

Rising 17 stories above one of Taipei's principal promenades, Dunhua Tower redefines the residential high-rise typology through a sophisticated interplay of materiality, geometry, and sustainable design. The tower's distinctive L-shaped footprint creates two contrasting facades—one slender and elegantly proportioned, the other broader and more commanding—allowing the building to respond dynamically to its urban context while maximizing natural light and views for residents. Housing 45 residential units, the building achieves an intimate scale that distinguishes it from the typical density of Taipei's housing market.

title: Plaza Salamero: Infrastructure, Landscape, and City / Hector Fernández Elorza
text:
Plaza Salamero: Infrastructure, Landscape, and City / Hector Fernández Elorza

The remodeling of Plaza de Salamero arose from a public competition launched by the Zaragoza City Council to replace the roof slab of the existing underground parking garage beneath the square, following a structural failure detected in 2020. Rather than viewing this circumstance as a limitation, the project turns it into an opportunity to redefine the public space and create a new urban park for the historic center.
